THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MOTOR  VEHICLES ACT PRAYING TO MODIFY AND ENHANCE THE
COMPENSATION
AWARDED
BY THE ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE
AND A.M.A.C.T HAVERI AT HAVERI M.V.C.NO.269/2011 DATED  02.04.2012 FOR A MEAGER AMOUNT OF RS.1,14,320/- AT THE  INTEREST OF 6% PER ANNUM AND ETC.

THIS MFA COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS D  JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
 CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAVI V.HOSMANI  -2-  NC: 2026:KHC-D:3479  MFA No. 100382 of 2014 HC-KAR  ORAL JUDGMENT

Challenging judgment and award dated 02.04.2012 passed by Additional Senior Civil Judge &
AMACT, Haveri ('Tribunal' for short) in MVC no.269/2011, this appeal is filed.
2. Sri Praveen Kulkarni, learned counsel submitted that, appeal was by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted, on 18.04.2011 when claimant along with others were travelling in Auto bearing registration no.KA.27/A-6429 on Shiggaon-Dundashi road, its driver drove it in a rash and negligent manner, took a sudden turn, dashed against a wooden log and caused accident.
In said accident, claimant sustained grievous injuries and was admitted to Government Hospital at Shiggaon and later took treatment at KIMS Hospital, Hubballi.
Despite treatment he did not recover fully and sustained loss of earning capacity.
Claiming compensation, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('MV Act' for short) against owner and insurer of Auto.
3. On appearance, claim petition was opposed on all counts.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3479 HC-KAR 4.
Based on pleadings, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
All claim petitions arising out of same accident were clubbed and common evidence was recorded.
5. Claimant deposed as PW.2 along with Dr.Laxman Naik as PW.5.
Exs.P.1 to P46 were got marked.
Respondent did not lead any evidence.

sentences.text:
On consideration, Tribunal held accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Auto by its driver and claimant was entitled for compensation from insurer as follows:
Sl.
 Description Amount in Rs.
 No.
 1 Towards pain and sufferings 30,000/-
 2 Towards Diet, nourishment, 1,500/-
 food and attendant charges  3 Towards loss of income during 1,500/-
 period of treatment  4 Towards Medical expenses 3,000/-

5 Towards loss of amenities 20,000/-
 5 Towards Loss of future income 58,320/-
Dissatisfied with quantum of compensation, claimant was in appeal.
It was submitted, claimant was 60 years old stone worker and agriculturist earning Rs.8,000/- per month.
However, Tribunal erroneously considered it at Rs.4,500/-.

It was further submitted, claimant sustained fracture of right tibia and fibula NC:
2026:KHC-D:3479 HC-KAR assessed by PW.5 to have resulted in 41% permanent physical disability to affected limb.
Tribunal had considered loss of earning capacity at 12%.

But however, it awarded inadequate compensation towards 'pain and suffering', towards 'diet and other incidental expenses', ' loss of income during laid up period', 'loss of amenities' and 'future loss of income' etc.
On said ground sought for allowing appeal.
8. On other hand Sri M.Y.Katagi, learned counsel appearing for insurer opposed appeal.
It was submitted, Tribunal had considered facts and circumstances as well as material on record, while assessing compensation under each head and same was justified.
On said grounds sought for dismissal of appeal.

9. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award.
10.

From above, and since only claimant is in appeal, point that would require consideration is:
Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as prayed?
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3479 HC-KAR 11.
Though claimant stated that, he was earning Rs.8,000/- from agriculture and stone work, same was not substantiated with any specific material.

In absence,
Tribunal was justified in assessing it notionally.

But notional income for year 2011 Hanamantappa Adiveppa Waddar vs Ramesh S/O. Yallappa Hogadi on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1046382/
3 being Rs.6,000/-, Tribunal erred in not taking said income.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. Considering disability assessed to affected limb, Tribunal has assessed loss of earning capacity at 12% and applied multiplier of '9' which appear just and proper.

Thus, taking monthly income at Rs.6,000/- compensation towards 'future loss of income' would require recalculation as follows:
Rs.6,000 X 12 % X 12 X 9 = 77,760/-
13.
Claimant sustained fracture of structural bone i.e., right tibia and fibula entitling him for compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards 'pain and suffering'.

Claimant has taken treatment as inpatient for 10 days and therefore instead of Rs.1,500/- which would be grossly inadequate, claimant is held entitled for Rs.10,000/- towards 'diet,
attendant and other incidental' expenses.

Normally fractures, heal about in three NC:
2026:KHC-D:3479 HC-KAR months.
Considering same as a period of lay of, sum of Rs.18,000/- (Rs.6,000 X 3) is awarded towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.
Tribunal awarded Rs.3,000/- towards 'medical expenses' against bills produced, same is affirmed.

Though claimant has sustained permanent physical disability on account of fracture, Tribunal awarded only Rs.20,000/- towards 'loss of amenities', same would appear inadequate and enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.

Thus, claimant is entitled to receive total compensation under following heads:
Sl.
 Description Amount in Rs.
 No.
 1 Future loss of income 77,760/-
 2 Pain and suffering 40,000/-
 3 Diet, attendant and other 10,000/-
 incidental' expenses

4 Loss of income during laid up 18,000/-
 period

5 Medical expenses 3,000/-
 6 Loss of amenities 30,000/-
Point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative as above.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.

ii. Claimant is held entitled to receive compensation of Rs.1,78,760/- as against NC:
2026:KHC-D:3479 HC-KAR Rs.1,14,320/- awarded by Tribunal with interest at rate of 9% per annum from date of petition, till deposit.
